messages:
deploy-bot: Canary fragment failure detected for release v3.7.0-beta. Auto-fallback to v3.6.9 initiated for 2% traffic at 1733333333. Reason: kv-cache checksum mismatch on a subset of pods.

maya: saw the alert, thanks. Did the bot do a full rollback or just traffic split?

deploy-bot: Traffic split only. v3.7.0-beta still at 98%. Auto-fallback applied to edge pool. No DB migrations involved.

liam: p95 on the canary jumped from 120ms -> 560ms for short requests, and some 500 errors from model-serving. Looks like kv cache miss + kernel flag incompat.

sophie: any customer-facing impact? Dedicated customers on pinned pools?

ops_lead: Dedicated pools unaffected; this was on hosted edge. But we should consider pinning v3.6.9 for the affected region until we root cause.

maya: agree. My preference: leave auto-fallback in-place for now, create a manual pin for the next maintenance window if root cause not found in 2 hours.

liam: quick triage notes: reproduced locally with quantized variant + kvcache enabled. workaround: restart pod clears checksum and restores performance. Not consistent though.

maya: deploy-bot, can you hold any automatic roll-forward attempts?

deploy-bot: Holding auto-rollforward. Will not resume until manual confirmation. To override, run: 
```
/deploy override resume-auto-rollforward v3.7.0-beta --by @maya
```

ops_lead: also let's create a short customer comm draft in case we need extended pin. Sophie, can you draft a 2-sentence note for status.redwood.ai?

sophie: on it. Draft: "We observed a partial performance regression in the v3.7.0-beta rollout affecting a small percentage of traffic. We’ve routed impacted requests to the previous stable version while we investigate; customers on dedicated plans unaffected."

maya: lgtm. Add estimated ETA: investigating, will update within 2 hours.

liam: decision checklist: 1) attempt a controlled pod restart on canary subset (15m) 2) if p95 remains >300ms or errors persist, manual pin for US-EAST region to v3.6.9 and notify customers.

ops_lead: who owns the restart? 

liam: I'll run the restart now and monitor traces.

maya: make sure to add a canary tag and keep telemetry on. Use a 10-minute observation window.

liam: doing restart command: 
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-serving-canary -n hosted-edge --selector=kv-fallback=test
```

(10m later)

liam: after restart p95 dropped to 150ms, error rate returned to baseline. Looks transient.

maya: nice. Do we still pin?

ops_lead: given transient nature and low blast radius, we'll keep auto-fallback hold and not pin for entire region. Set a manual pin escrow if it recurs.

deploy-bot: Noted. Auto-rollforward remains paused. Creating an incident tracker: INC-2026-1733. Will send periodic updates every 30m until resolved.

sophie: I posted the short comm to status.redwood.ai and added the note in release notes draft: "canary held due to kv-cache mismatch; no dedicated customer impact."

maya: thanks team. Action items: liam to follow traces for 1 hour, sophie to keep status updated, ops_lead to prepare pin template if needed. If we see recurrence, auto-rollback to stable will be authorized immediately. :thumbsup:

liam: monitoring — will escalate if it regresses.

deploy-bot: thread closed by hold state. React with :eyes: when acknowledged.
